description: An elderly man in a patterned cloth wrap, a coral-bead necklace and a gold-trimmed cap kneels in a dim earthen workshop and pours glowing molten metal from a crucible with tongs into a rough clay mould. Behind him on a shelf stand gold-coloured cast heads and figures, with a charcoal furnace, pots, tools and a second worker at a fire on the left. Smoke rises and there are no letters or frame; a small sparkle logo sits in the bottom-right corner.
reason: Shows a traditional metal caster pouring molten metal into a clay mould in a pre-industrial workshop, but the card is the 1954 IBM machine translation demonstration in New York. Nothing in the picture is a computer, office or 1950s setting.
